faqs.q: An opossum has moved in under my Danville porch — is that a problem?
faqs.a: A passing opossum eating snails and fallen fruit is harmless, but one denning under a porch or in a crawlspace in Danville fouls the space and will be reused by the next animal. Opossums are not a rabies-vector species here, despite the fierce display when cornered. Our crew removes the animal at the property under permit, cleans the den area, and seals the gap it used.

Danville.wildlife_intro:
Danville's river-bluff mill neighborhoods and older suburbs close Virginia's Southside in Danville. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: dan River and its mill districts, historic tobacco warehouses, Anglers Park woods. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Danville — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
